backend.vigem.title: ViGEmBus Driver
backend.vigem.err.driver-missing.title: ViGEmBus driver not detected
backend.vigem.err.driver-missing.body: ViGEmBus is a kernel driver that lets Satellite create a virtual Xbox 360 controller on Windows. Without it, controller input cannot be forwarded.
backend.vigem.err.driver-missing.step3: A restart may be required. Check Device Manager under "System devices" for "Nefarius Virtual Gamepad Emulation Bus"
backend.vigem.err.driver-missing.step4: Refresh this page; status should show "Detected"
backend.vigem.err.bus-open-failed.title: ViGEmBus driver detected but unresponsive
backend.vigem.err.bus-open-failed.body: The driver is installed but Satellite could not open the bus. This usually means a version mismatch between the driver and the satellite build, or the driver service is stopped.
backend.vigem.err.bus-open-failed.step2: Or restart your machine and try again
backend.uinput.title: uinput Backend
backend.uinput.err.device-missing.title: /dev/uinput not found
backend.uinput.err.device-missing.body: The uinput kernel module ships with every mainline Linux kernel but may not be loaded right now. Without it, Satellite cannot create virtual gamepads.
backend.uinput.err.permission-denied.bod: /dev/uinput exists but the user running Satellite cannot write to it. Add a udev rule and join the input group.
backend.uinput.err.permission-denied.ste: Add yourself to the input group
Log out and back in for the group change to apply, then refresh this page
backend.hidmaestro.title: HIDMaestro Driver
backend.hidmaestro.err.driver-missing.bo: HIDMaestro is a user-mode driver that lets Satellite create virtual DualSense, Switch Pro, DualShock 4 and Xbox 360 controllers on Windows. Without it those controller types cannot be created.
backend.hidmaestro.err.driver-missing.st: Re-run the Satellite installer and keep the "HIDMaestro driver" component selected
The driver installs without a reboot; approve the elevation prompt when asked
Refresh this page; status should show "Detected"
backend.hidmaestro.err.helper-missing.bo: satellite-hm-helper.exe is missing next to satellite.exe. Satellite uses it to create HIDMaestro virtual controllers.
backend.hidmaestro.err.helper-missing.st: Re-install Satellite and keep the "HIDMaestro driver" component selected
Refresh this page; status should show "Detected"

devices.touchpad.tip: Where this device's DualSense / DS4 touchpad is routed on this host. Set on the client (dish app); this dashboard reflects the current selection.

motion.on.title: Gyro and accelerometer are streaming to the virtual gamepad.
motion.nosink.title: Motion is captured from the controller but not delivered: the virtual device has no IMU surface to receive it (an Xbox-typed device, a ViGEmBus older than 1.22, or the macOS backend).

settings.udp-port.label: UDP Port
settings.udp-port.error: UDP port must be a whole number between 1024 and 65535.
settings.udp-port.rejected: Server rejected the UDP port. Keeping %1$s.
settings.discovery.title: Discovery
settings.discovery.hint: mDNS / Bonjour is the modern discovery path and works on subnets that drop broadcast. The legacy UDP beacon stays on as a fallback for senders that predate the mDNS responder. Turn it off only on a network where every sender supports mDNS.
settings.crash.title: Diagnostics
settings.crash.label: Send crash reports
settings.crash.hint: Off by default. When on, Satellite sends a report to its developers if it crashes: the stack trace, the version and the operating system. It never sends your gameplay, your controller input, your paired devices or the contents of your network. Turning it off stops the very next report, not just future ones.
settings.crash.status.off: Crash reports are not being sent.
settings.crash.status.unavailable: This build cannot send crash reports, so nothing is being sent. Official releases can.
settings.audio.title: Controller audio
settings.audio.label: Controller microphone and speaker
settings.audio.hint: A DualSense or DualShock 4 v2 created here also gets the controller's own microphone and speaker, as real Windows audio devices. Windows decides what plays through them, the same as for any headset: pick the controller under Settings > System > Sound > Volume mixer for the apps you want on it. Controller audio needs a bundled signed kernel USB transport, which HIDMaestro installs the first time such a controller is created. Turn this off to keep the input-only controller and skip that install. Changes apply the next time a controller is connected.
settings.audio.mic-label: Microphone: your voice reaches the game
settings.audio.speaker-label: Speaker: game audio reaches your headset
settings.audio.directions-hint: Each direction can be turned off on its own. The controller keeps both Windows audio devices either way; the switch only stops the audio crossing the network, so it applies straight away instead of waiting for the next connection.
settings.audio.keep-default-label: Keep my current default playback device
settings.audio.keep-default-hint: Windows makes any newly connected audio device the default, which would send every sound on this PC to the controller. With this on, Satellite puts your previous device back afterwards. Turn it off if you want the controller to become the default the way Windows intended.

donate.title: Support Satellite
donate.h1: Satellite runs on coffee and goodwill.
donate.lead: Satellite, Dish, and every Dish client are free, open source, ad-free, and analytics-free. No paywalled features, no upsells, and no plans for any of that. Donations are what keep them true.
donate.pill.headline: Support Satellite
donate.ways.title: Ways to give
donate.tiers.sponsors.label: GitHub Sponsors
donate.tiers.sponsors.blurb: Monthly sponsorship, processed by GitHub. No platform cut, and the only option GitHub matches dollar-for-dollar through the Sponsors Matching Fund where eligible.
donate.tiers.kofi.label: Ko-fi
donate.tiers.kofi.blurb: Tip jar. Buy us a coffee, no account required. Ko-fi takes 0% on one-time tips, so every dollar reaches the project.
donate.tiers.kofi.currencies: Card, Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal
donate.tiers.bmac.label: Buy Me a Coffee
donate.tiers.bmac.blurb: Quick one-time gift or a monthly membership. Card, Apple Pay, or Google Pay. Great if you don't have a GitHub account.
donate.why.title: What your donation actually pays for
donate.why.hosting: Hosting. dish.tinkernorth.com, tinkernorth.com, and every signed-installer mirror.
donate.why.signing: Code-signing certificates. Windows SmartScreen only plays nice because we pay for an EV certificate every year, and the same goes for the Apple Developer Program account for the upcoming macOS client.
donate.why.play: Google Play developer fee. Plus the time required to keep the Play listing compliant with every new policy round.
donate.why.hardware: Hardware testing. Phones across the Android version range, gaming PCs at different tiers, and the controllers we benchmark against.
donate.why.time: Time. Honest answer: most of it. This is a nights-and-weekends project. Donations let me say "yes" to working on it instead of taking on extra consulting.
donate.faq.title: Donation FAQ
donate.faq.where.q: Where does the money actually go?
donate.faq.where.a: Code-signing certificates, the Google Play developer fee, hosting, the eventual Apple Developer Program account for Dish for macOS, domain renewals, and the time I'd otherwise spend taking contract work instead of shipping.
donate.faq.nonprofit.a: No. TinkerNorth is an independent maker, so donations are not tax-deductible. They're treated as gifts.
donate.faq.which.a: GitHub Sponsors if you can. It takes 0% platform fees on individual sponsorships and makes recurring support easy. Ko-fi is good for one-off tips. Buy Me a Coffee works if you'd rather pay with Apple or Google Pay and don't have a GitHub account.
donate.faq.perks.a: Nothing functional. Every feature, every release, every privacy guarantee is the same for sponsors and non-sponsors. What you get is a shout-out in the release notes for major versions and the knowledge that you're directly funding a free-as-in-freedom project.
donate.faq.cant.q: I can't donate. How else can I help?
donate.faq.cant.a: Star the repos on GitHub, file good bug reports, contribute a PR, write a blog post or video, or just tell a friend who's been hunting for a wireless gamepad solution.
donate.other.title: Can't donate? You can still help.
donate.other.star: Star the Satellite repo and the Dish for Android repo on GitHub. It genuinely moves the needle for discovery.
donate.other.bugs: File good bug reports. A reproducible issue is worth ten "doesn't work" threads.
donate.other.tell: Tell a friend. A single post or short video is worth a lot.
donate.other.contribute: Contribute. Pull requests are welcome on every repo. See CONTRIBUTING.md. Translations are especially easy to land.
donate.thanks: Thank you. Every dollar, every star, every shared link. They all add up. ~Emir
